pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

This PR contains several changes to allow users to fetch newly created dashboards and folders. 

The changes are:
* on client side: remove the use of authLib cache when running authZ service in-proc
* on server side: add a denial cache to return quickly when we know that a user does not have permission on a specific resource
* on server side: if permission denial cache is not hit, and the requested resource is not found in cached permissions, requery permissions from the DB

**Why do we need this feature?**

Otherwise dash/folder creator can't access the dashboard/folder that they've just created.

**Who is this feature for?**

Grafana users

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/identity-access-team/issues/1316
pr.title: AuthZService: improve authz caching

raw_findings.body: permissionCacheUsage is recorded with cache_hit="false" even though the permission cache actually contained an entry for the user/action, undercounting real cache hit rate and skewing cache-effectiveness metrics/dashboards.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cache observability metrics misreport actual cache utilization, potentially leading to incorrect capacity/TTL tuning decisions based on inaccurate hit-rate data.
raw_findings.impact: permissionCacheUsage is recorded with cache_hit="false" even though the permission cache actually contained an entry for the user/action, undercounting real cache hit rate and skewing cache-effectiveness metrics/dashboards.
raw_findings.root_cause: The metric label at this line is derived from the outcome of the permission decision rather than from whether the cache lookup itself succeeded.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Base the permissionCacheUsage label strictly on whether getCachedIdentityPermissions returned data (err == nil), independent of the final allowed/denied outcome, e.g. record "true" immediately after a successful cache lookup regardless of the subsequent checkPermission result.
raw_findings.title: Cache hit incorrectly recorded as cache miss when cached permissions do not grant access
raw_findings.trigger: getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cached permissions (err == nil) but checkPermission determines the cached scope map does not grant the requested resource, so execution falls through past the cache branch to the DB query.

raw_findings.body: The retried Check() immediately returns Allowed:false straight from permDenialCache without re-evaluating current permissions, denying access to a resource the user now legitimately has permission for, for up to 30 seconds — reintroducing a variant of the exact staleness problem this PR was meant to fix (inability to access newly permissioned/created resources).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Users can be incorrectly denied access to resources they have valid permission for, for up to the cache TTL duration.
raw_findings.impact: The retried Check() immediately returns Allowed:false straight from permDenialCache without re-evaluating current permissions, denying access to a resource the user now legitimately has permission for, for up to 30 seconds — reintroducing a variant of the exact staleness problem this PR was meant to fix (inability to access newly permissioned/created resources).
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly added denial cache short-circuits Check() before any freshness re-verification and has no invalidation path tied to permission changes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not let the denial cache short-circuit unconditionally; e.g. use a much shorter TTL for denial entries, or invalidate/skip the denial cache entry whenever the underlying permission set for that user/namespace changes (mirroring how the positive-permission fallback already re-queries the DB).
raw_findings.title: New permission denial cache can mask newly granted access for up to the cache TTL
raw_findings.trigger: A prior Check() call for a specific user/namespace/action/resource-name/parent-folder combination is denied and cached in permDenialCache; within shortCacheTTL (30s) the user is subsequently granted permission on that exact resource (e.g. via role assignment or resource creation), and the same Check() request is retried.

raw_findings.body: Existing tests (e.g. TestService_CacheCheck) only pre-populate permDenialCache manually to test the read/short-circuit path; the write path that actually populates the denial cache from a real DB-verified deny is never exercised, so a regression (wrong key, wrong TTL, or the Set call being skipped) would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent regressions in denial-cache population logic could pass CI undetected, degrading the effectiveness or correctness of the new caching feature without being noticed.
raw_findings.impact: Existing tests (e.g. TestService_CacheCheck) only pre-populate permDenialCache manually to test the read/short-circuit path; the write path that actually populates the denial cache from a real DB-verified deny is never exercised, so a regression (wrong key, wrong TTL, or the Set call being skipped) would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: New denial-cache write behavior introduced in Check() was not accompanied by a test covering that specific code path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test case that triggers a genuine deny via the store, then asserts the expected key exists in s.permDenialCache, or that a second identical Check() call short-circuits without additional calls to the underlying store.
raw_findings.title: No test covers that Check() populates the permission denial cache after a genuine DB-confirmed denial
raw_findings.trigger: A Check() call results in a genuine DB-confirmed denial (no cached data, real permission query returns not-allowed).

finding.verifier_reason: The metric at line 137 is intentionally recording a cache miss because the code falls through to the DB query path. When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns data (err == nil) but checkPermission returns allowed=false, the code does NOT return early - it proceeds to call getIdentityPermissions (DB query) at line 139. The 'false' label correctly indicates the cache did not satisfy the request, requiring a DB fallback. This is correct behavior, not a bug.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch introduces permDenialCache at lines 117-121 that short-circuits Check() returning Allowed:false without re-verifying permissions. The cache has shortCacheTTL (30s) and no invalidation mechanism tied to permission changes. If a user is denied, then granted permission within 30s, the cached denial will incorrectly block access. This is a valid staleness concern introduced by the new code.
